solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Weaver a couple of times involved in success

indicators.note: being involved in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a boom is a period of great success or prosperity
T is the abbreviation for time, so two times give two Ts

explanation.surface: A cloth-weaver who has been twice involved in a thriving business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaver' is not a textile worker but Nick Bottom, the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, who is given an ass's head, is named Nick Bottom.

clue.text: Dodgy judge dismissed in instant

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so this letter leaves the word it was part of

parts.note: a jiffy is an instant, a very short moment

explanation.surface: A shady judge is sacked on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal adjectives for something doubtful, unreliable or of questionable quality.

clue.text: Large group excursion initially stays around right inns

parts.note: a host is a large number of people, as in a heavenly host

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word excursion
around tells us the word for stays is wrapped about the abbreviation for right

parts.note: lies means stays or remains, as in 'the book lies on the table'

explanation.surface: A big party on an outing first puts up at various pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R inside LIES to make LRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelries are old-fashioned or jocular words for pubs and lodging houses that serve travellers.

clue.text: Sonorous 24? Almost seduced internally

indicators.note: internally means placed within, so the trimmed word goes inside the word from the other clue

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, a musical number

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: to undo someone was an old way of saying to seduce or ruin them, giving undid

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a breathless remark about near-seduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undo' in its old sense of seduce or ruin; 'Almost' drops the last letter and 'internally' puts the rest within the answer to 24.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding voice or instrument is resonant and full, the same as a sonorous one.

clue.text: End is sinking, rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: in snooker or pool, sinking a ball is potting it, so pots means sinks

explanation.surface: A grim forecast: the end comes as one goes under, or as one climbs back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinking' is the snooker sense: a player who pots a ball sinks it into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to bring it to a halt, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Supporting no carbon — thus father does for bicarbonate

indicators.note: no means without, so the chemical symbol is removed from the word for supporting

parts.note: backing means supporting, as in backing a candidate
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
so means thus, as in 'and so it ended'
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a backing with the carbon stripped out stands in for bicarbonate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does for' is a link meaning 'serves as'. There is a joke in removing carbon on the way to bicarbonate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate is the kitchen raising agent sold under the everyday name used in baking.

clue.text: Tell institute to retain most of dealings

indicators.note: to retain something is to hold it within, so the trimmed word sits inside the abbreviation
most of means all but the last letter of the word for dealings

parts.note: truck means dealings, as in 'have no truck with someone'

explanation.surface: Someone instructs an institution to keep hold of most of its business affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'truck' in the sense of dealings survives in the phrase 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone to do something is to order or direct them, the same as instructing them.

clue.text: Sick of quartet imprisoning officer

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the officer is shut within the number

parts.note: a quartet is a group of four
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up with a group of four who have locked up an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' sits at the front looking like the subject's mood; it is the definition, and 'of' is a piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off colour is an informal idiom for being slightly unwell, which is what sick means here.

clue.text: Man, note, behind front of stalls?

indicators.note: behind says the note comes after the theatre seating row, so it is placed second

parts.note: the front row of a theatre's stalls is labelled row A

explanation.surface: A theatre usher points out a man sitting right behind the first row.
explanation.walkthrough: The front of a theatre's stalls is ROW A, the seats nearest the stage; N for note comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowan is a male first name, as borne by the comic actor Rowan Atkinson, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Pressure to ignore special tutor

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the abbreviation is dropped from the word

parts.note: strain means pressure or stress

explanation.surface: A tutor is urged to ignore the pressure of special cases.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor someone is to teach or coach them, which is also what training them means.

clue.text: Meeting test, getting only second half of it

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: only the second half of the word means just its last two letters are kept

parts.note: it refers back to the word test in the clue

explanation.surface: A meeting where an exam is cut short halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' means the word 'test' itself, whose second half gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic meeting arranged between lovers.

clue.text: Fresh cycle race in sports pages and much else

parts.note: new means fresh
a sprint is a short track cycling race

explanation.surface: A new cycling event features in the sports coverage, alongside plenty of other items.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers are printed on cheap paper, which carries the sports pages along with every other section.

clue.text: Squabbling partners claim a line's out of place

indicators.note: letters out of place have been moved about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: the 's here is the word is, but it supplies the letter S of the fodder

explanation.surface: A quarrelling couple, one insisting the other's remark is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is part of the fodder: CLAIM A LINES rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A misalliance is an unsuitable marriage or partnership, typically one where the couple quarrel.

clue.text: Linda feels conflicted, exhibiting this?

indicators.note: conflicted means torn or in turmoil, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Linda is torn between wanting something and holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a woman feeling conflicted may be showing restraint over her wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Being torn between desire and restraint is the inner struggle of someone denying herself a pleasure.

clue.text: Wasting US spies, infiltrating English with breeding

indicators.note: spies infiltrating an organisation get inside it, so these letters go within the rest

parts.note: mating is breeding, as of animals
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: American agents work their way into an English stud farm, slowly losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' places CIA inside EMATING, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasting disease makes the body thin and gaunt, which is what an emaciating one does.

clue.text: Weapon, mostly twisted does for animal

indicators.note: mostly twisted means the greater part of the word is turned around, its last two letters swapped

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A firearm that has been bent out of shape serves as a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Only most of GUN is turned: UN becomes NU, after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Emsworth, say, I note engaged in pig keeping

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the word for pig

parts.note: a hog is a pig
Lord Emsworth is the pig-loving peer in P G Wodehouse's Blandings novels; Ld is short for Lord

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's Lord Emsworth is busy tending his prize pig.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Emsworth, of P G Wodehouse's Blandings stories, dotes on his pig, but here he simply stands for a lord, LD.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding and keeping both mean retaining possession of something.

clue.text: End of run in Swiss city avoiding Lake

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'is she in?'

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so the abbreviation is left out of the city name

parts.note: Basle is the English spelling of the Swiss city Basel
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A runner ends up in a Swiss city, steering well clear of the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is a baseball run, not a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a run is scored when the runner gets back to the plate where batting starts, so it is a run's finish.

clue.text: Salesman in Florida going full tilt?

parts.note: a tout is a pushy seller, as of tickets

explanation.surface: A hard-selling salesman in Florida working at full speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going flat out means moving or working at maximum speed or effort.

clue.text: France's aircraft descending in part of Europe

parts.note: F is the international vehicle registration letter for France
aircraft coming down to land can be called landers

explanation.surface: French planes coming down somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is a historic region of north-west Europe, now mostly in Belgium.

clue.text: Wet earth in odd parts of mound

indicators.note: odd parts of means the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Damp soil found in odd places within a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud is soil mixed with water, the soft wet ground underfoot.

clue.text: I give marker to graduate back filling unsettled class's study periods

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the reversed run sits within the rearranged letters
unsettled means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word class, its 's a link meaning has

indicators.note: back means the run of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: a tab is a small marker, such as a label on a file
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A teacher hands a graduate a marker as a restless class goes back to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run I, marker, graduate round to ABBATI; 'filling' sets that inside SCALS, made from 'unsettled' class.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabbaticals are periods of paid leave granted to academics for research or study.

clue.text: Ready impudence

definitions.meaning: ready, as in readies, is slang for cash or money

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang both words mean money, and the same word also means brazen cheek or nerve.

clue.text: Scanty spring growth I ignored

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter I is dropped

parts.note: a rise is a growth or increase

explanation.surface: Spring growth is thin on the ground, and I take no notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring growth' looks like new shoots; it is two pieces, SPA and RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse and scanty both mean thinly scattered or meagre in amount.

clue.text: Unpleasant resistance about new park feature

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abbreviation for new goes within the word for unpleasant

parts.note: bad means unpleasant
to make a stand is to put up resistance

explanation.surface: Nasty opposition to a new feature in the local park.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandstand is a covered outdoor platform for musicians, often found in public parks.

clue.text: Number in G and S that's picked up?

definitions.text: Number in G and S that's picked up?

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, so the letters read from the bottom upwards
in means placed inside, so the abbreviation goes between the two letters

explanation.surface: A tune from a Gilbert and Sullivan opera that people pick up easily.
explanation.walkthrough: G and S is Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of comic operas; their numbers are songs, and catchy ones get picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical number in a show is a song, and tunes are picked up by those who hear them.

clue.text: Scientist ignites laboratory packages

indicators.note: packages means wraps up inside, so the words contain the scientist's name

explanation.surface: A scientist sets fire to parcels in the laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packages' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer behind alternating-current systems.

clue.text: Sun near sunset is not bright

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for sun, as for Sunday
near sunset the sun is low in the sky

explanation.surface: The sun close to setting is losing its brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow is an informal word for dull-witted, the opposite of bright in the sense of clever.

clue.text: Proust hero, pale, seated between bridge players

indicators.note: seated between means placed in the middle, so the word for pale sits between the two letters

parts.note: in bridge the partners are named by compass points, here South and North
in bridge the partners are named by compass points, here South and North
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Proust's hero, looking pallid, sits at the card table between two partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Swann is a central character in Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time, giving his name to Swann's Way.

clue.text: Playing our tune on board ship with difficulty

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the rearranged letters go between its two letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: playing a tune can mean playing about with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band strikes up a tune aboard a ship as it makes heavy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' gives TRENUOU from the two words, and 'on board' puts it between the steamship's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strenuous takes great effort, so a task done with difficulty is a strenuous one.
